description: The core Formation Feed collection for Reforged. A Scripture-first discovery feed whose cards move the reader toward reading the Bible in context, prayer, memorization, reflection, community, and obedient response to grace.
editorialPrinciples: Scripture is primary. Every card exposes surrounding context so passages are never proof-texted in isolation.
Truth cards summarize what Scripture teaches. They point back to the text and never replace it.
Practices are grace-motivated responses to what God has done, not ways to earn His favor.
Identity is grounded in union with Christ, and sanctification is presented as real, gradual growth that God empowers.
Suffering is treated honestly, without simplistic explanations, and lament is welcomed as faithful prayer.
No engagement bait, no public metrics. Every card should lead toward reading, prayer, memorization, reflection, community, or obedience.
No Bible text is stored here. Cards carry references only, and the app renders the reader's selected translation.

cards.title: Be still before God
cards.prompt: What would it look like to stop striving for control and remember who God is?

cards.title: The Lord is my shepherd
cards.prompt: Where do you most need to trust that the Shepherd is with you, even in the valley?

cards.title: Do not be anxious
cards.prompt: What request have you been carrying that you could bring to God with thanksgiving right now?

cards.title: Come to me, all who are weary
cards.prompt: What weight are you carrying that Jesus is inviting you to bring to Him?

cards.title: In Christ, a new creation
cards.prompt: If you are truly a new creation in Christ, what old label are you ready to lay down?

cards.title: No condemnation for those in Christ
cards.prompt: What accusation do you keep hearing that the verdict of the gospel has already answered?

cards.title: Abide in the vine
cards.prompt: Where have you been trying to bear fruit apart from staying close to Jesus?

cards.title: Ask, seek, knock
cards.prompt: What have you stopped asking God for because the waiting felt too long?

cards.title: Pray like this
cards.prompt: Pray the Lord's Prayer slowly. Which line does your heart most need today?

cards.title: Be holy, for He is holy
cards.prompt: Holiness flows from being ransomed. What area of life are you ready to set apart for God?

cards.title: He is faithful to forgive
cards.prompt: What is one thing you can bring into the light, trusting that confession leads to cleansing?

cards.title: God provides a way out
cards.prompt: Where do you need to look for the escape God has already provided?

cards.title: Stand in the armor of God
cards.prompt: The strength is His, not yours. Which piece of the armor do you most need to take up today?

cards.title: Trust in the Lord, not your own understanding
cards.prompt: What decision are you leaning on your own understanding to solve?

cards.title: Ask God for wisdom
cards.prompt: God gives wisdom generously and without reproach. What will you ask Him for today?

cards.title: Forgive as you were forgiven
cards.prompt: How does remembering how much you have been forgiven change how you see the person who hurt you?

cards.title: Go and be reconciled
cards.prompt: Is there a conversation you have been avoiding that love would ask you to have gently?

cards.title: Blessed are the peacemakers
cards.prompt: Peacemaking is more than avoiding conflict. Where could you actively pursue peace this week?

cards.title: Bear one another's burdens
cards.prompt: Whose burden could you help carry, and whose help do you need to accept?

cards.title: Stir one another toward love
cards.prompt: Who in your life is God calling you to spur on, and how might you do it this week?

cards.title: The greatest is the servant
cards.prompt: Jesus served to the point of the cross. Where is He inviting you to serve without recognition?

cards.title: Count others more significant
cards.prompt: Whose interests is God asking you to look to today above your own?

cards.title: Godliness with contentment
cards.prompt: What would change if you truly believed that godliness with contentment is great gain?

cards.title: Give thanks in everything
cards.prompt: This calls for thanks in every circumstance, not for every circumstance. What can you thank God for even now?

cards.title: Blessed are those who mourn
cards.prompt: What grief do you need to let yourself feel honestly before the God who comforts?

cards.title: We do not lose heart
cards.prompt: What unseen and eternal reality can steady you in a season that feels like wasting away?

cards.title: Count trials as joy
cards.prompt: This is joy in the outcome God is working, not pretending the trial does not hurt. What is God forming in you?

cards.title: Run with endurance, eyes on Jesus
cards.prompt: What weight is slowing you down, and how does looking to Jesus help you lay it aside?

cards.title: Go and make disciples
cards.prompt: Jesus sends you with His authority and His presence. Who is one person He has placed near you?

cards.title: Work as for the Lord
cards.prompt: How would you approach today's work differently if you did it heartily for the Lord?

cards.title: Remember the Sabbath
cards.prompt: Rest is rooted in trusting God to sustain the world without you. What keeps you from stopping?

cards.title: God is not distant in trouble
cards.body: God does not promise a trouble-free life. He calls Himself a present refuge in the middle of it.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What trouble do you need to bring to God plainly today?

cards.title: Your standing rests on Christ, not your record
cards.body: In Christ you are chosen and accepted before you have done anything to prove yourself. Your worst day does not lower this, and your best day does not raise it.
cards.reflectionPrompt: Where have you been measuring your standing with God by your performance?

cards.title: You are adopted, not on trial
cards.body: The gospel does not leave you an anxious defendant. Through faith God makes you His child and gives you His Spirit, so you can come to Him as Father.
cards.reflectionPrompt: How would coming to God as a beloved child change your prayers today?

cards.title: Prayer is dependence, not performance
cards.body: God is not impressed by polished words. He welcomes honest, humble prayer, and His Spirit helps you even when you do not know what to say.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What would you pray if you knew God wanted honesty more than eloquence?

cards.title: Repentance is a road home
cards.body: Turning from sin is not God's way of shaming you. His kindness leads you to repentance so you can walk in freedom, not fear.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What sin have you been avoiding because you feared God's response more than trusting His kindness?

cards.title: Sanctification is real growth, and it is slow
cards.body: God is committed to finishing the work He began in you. Growth is often gradual, and steady change by His Spirit is still change.
cards.reflectionPrompt: Where can you see slow growth that you might be tempted to dismiss?

cards.title: Temptation is not the same as sin
cards.body: Jesus was tempted in every way yet without sin, so being tempted does not make you guilty. Sin grows when desire is fed and acted on, so the moment to turn is early.
cards.reflectionPrompt: Where do you need to turn early, before a desire is fed?

cards.title: You were not made to fight sin alone
cards.body: God gives His people to one another so that no one stands unguarded. Confession and honest friendship are means of grace, not signs of weakness.
cards.reflectionPrompt: Who could you invite into an honest struggle you have been carrying alone?

cards.title: God gives wisdom to those who ask
cards.body: Wisdom is not reserved for the naturally clever. God gives it generously to those who ask in faith and are willing to obey what they hear.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What is one decision you can hand to God in prayer before you act on it?

cards.title: Forgiveness releases a debt
cards.body: To forgive is not to say the wound did not matter. It is to release the debt to God, trusting Him to be the just judge, because He first forgave you.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What debt are you still holding that God is inviting you to release to Him?

cards.title: Peace with people begins with peace from God
cards.body: Because you have peace with God through Christ, you can pursue peace with others without needing to win. So far as it depends on you, live at peace.
cards.reflectionPrompt: Where might your security in Christ free you to seek peace instead of victory?

cards.title: The church is a body, and you are needed
cards.body: You are not an optional part of the church. God has placed each member in the body on purpose, and no one can say to another that they are not needed.
cards.reflectionPrompt: How has God gifted you to serve the body you belong to?

cards.title: Greatness looks like service
cards.body: In God's kingdom, greatness is measured by humble service, not by status. Jesus washed feet and gave His life, and He calls His followers to do the same.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What lowly act of service could you take up gladly this week?

cards.title: Contentment is learned, not stumbled upon
cards.body: Paul learned to be content in plenty and in want, and the secret was strength from Christ. Contentment grows as you rest in Him rather than in circumstances.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What circumstance are you waiting to change before you allow yourself to be content?

cards.title: Gratitude remembers what God has done
cards.body: Thankfulness is not denial of hardship. It is the discipline of remembering God's benefits, which steadies the heart when much feels uncertain.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What benefit of God have you been forgetting lately?

cards.title: Lament is a faithful way to pray
cards.body: The Bible gives words for grief and complaint addressed to God. Lament does not doubt God's goodness. It brings pain to Him and waits for His steadfast love.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What sorrow could you speak honestly to God, ending in what you still know to be true of Him?

cards.title: Suffering is real, and it is not the last word
cards.body: Scripture never minimizes pain, yet it promises that present suffering will be outweighed by coming glory, when God wipes away every tear.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What promise of God's future do you need to hold onto in the middle of a hard season?

cards.title: Hidden Scripture becomes present help
cards.body: Verses stored in the heart are not just facts to recall. They become the Spirit's tools to guard you from sin and steady you in trial.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What single verse would help you most if it lived in your memory?

cards.title: Faithfulness in small things is not small
cards.body: God notices quiet, ordinary obedience. What looks minor to others is where much of discipleship happens, and He calls you not to grow weary in doing good.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What small, unseen obedience is God asking you to keep up?

cards.title: Ordinary work can be worship
cards.body: Whatever you do, in word or deed, can be done in the name of the Lord and for His glory. Your daily tasks are not separate from your walk with God.
cards.reflectionPrompt: How could you offer today's ordinary work to God as worship?

cards.title: The gospel is good news to carry, not a test to pass
cards.body: You witness as an ambassador, not a salesperson. The message is that God reconciles sinners to Himself in Christ, and its power does not depend on your polish.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What fear about sharing your faith would ease if you trusted the power of the message itself?

cards.title: Rest is trust that God keeps the world
cards.body: Sleep and Sabbath are acts of faith. You lie down because the God who never slumbers is the one holding everything together, not you.
cards.reflectionPrompt: What would you need to entrust to God in order to truly rest?

cards.title: Name the burden
cards.body: Take two quiet minutes. Name one burden to God without trying to solve it first.

cards.title: Pray one honest breath prayer
cards.body: Breathe slowly and pray a short line from Scripture, such as help me trust You. Repeat it until your body settles.

cards.title: Confess one thing plainly
cards.body: Name one sin to God clearly, without excuse or minimizing. Then receive His promise to forgive and cleanse.

cards.title: Set one guardrail today
cards.body: Choose one concrete boundary that removes an easy path to temptation, and put it in place before you need it.

cards.title: Reach out to your accountability partner
cards.body: Send one honest message to a trusted friend about how you are really doing. You do not need to have it all resolved first.

cards.title: Bring the decision to God first
cards.body: Before you weigh the options, pause and ask God for wisdom, telling Him you are willing to follow where He leads.
cards.completionLabel: I brought the decision to God

cards.title: Send one word of encouragement
cards.body: Think of someone who is weary and send them one specific, honest encouragement grounded in God's faithfulness.

cards.title: Do one hidden act of service
cards.body: Serve someone in a way no one will notice or thank you for. Let it be an offering seen by your Father.

cards.title: Count three gifts
cards.body: Write down three specific gifts from God today, small or large, and thank Him for each by name.

cards.title: Pray for someone who wronged you
cards.body: Bring to God, by name, someone who has hurt you. Ask for their good, and ask Him to soften your heart.

cards.title: Choose a verse to carry this week
cards.body: Pick one short verse to hide in your heart. Write it out, read it aloud, and begin reviewing it.

cards.title: Take a Sabbath hour
cards.body: Set aside one hour to stop producing. Rest, worship, or simply be with God, trusting Him to hold what you set down.

cards.title: Name one person and pray for them
cards.body: Name one person who does not yet know Jesus. Pray for them, and ask God for an open door and gracious words.

cards.title: Offer your work to God
cards.body: Before you begin your tasks, pray a short line offering your work to God and asking Him to establish it.

cards.title: Sit with a single passage
cards.body: Read one short passage slowly three times. Ask God to help you understand and obey one thing from it.

cards.title: Whose voice are you believing?
cards.body: Write one sentence you have been telling yourself. Then answer it with what God says in Scripture.
cards.journalPlaceholder: The thought I keep believing is... Scripture answers it by saying...

cards.title: Where do you feel unsafe with God?
cards.body: Name a place where you find it hard to trust God, and bring that specific fear honestly to Him.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I find it hard to trust God with... What might it look like to hand this to Him is...

cards.title: What are you trying to earn?
cards.body: Consider where you are striving to secure God's approval by effort, when the gospel says it is already given in Christ.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I keep trying to earn... The gospel tells me instead that...

cards.title: What have you stopped bringing to God?
cards.body: Notice a request or a part of your life you have quietly withdrawn from prayer, and consider why.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I have stopped praying about... I think that is because...

cards.title: What sin have you started calling normal?
cards.body: Ask God to search you and show one thing you have begun to excuse. His conviction is an invitation, not condemnation.
cards.journalPlaceholder: A sin I have been excusing is... I want to bring it to God by...

cards.title: Where are you tempted, and who knows?
cards.body: Consider the place you are most vulnerable to sin, and whether anyone is walking with you there.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I am most tempted when... One person I could tell is...

cards.title: What decision are you carrying alone?
cards.body: Name a choice you have been trying to solve by yourself, and consider whom God might use to give counsel.
cards.journalPlaceholder: A decision I am carrying alone is... Someone wise I could ask is...

cards.title: Who do you need to forgive?
cards.body: Name a person and what holds you back from releasing the debt. Ask God, who forgave you at great cost, for help.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I am holding something against... What makes forgiveness hard is...

cards.title: Where have you withdrawn from others?
cards.body: Notice where you have pulled back from fellow believers, and ask what a small step back toward community could be.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I have withdrawn from... One small step back toward others is...

cards.title: Where is God inviting you to serve unseen?
cards.body: Consider a need you could meet without anyone noticing, as an offering to the Father who sees in secret.
cards.journalPlaceholder: A quiet need I could meet is... What makes me want recognition is...

cards.title: What has your discontent been telling you?
cards.body: Listen to a recurring discontent and ask what it reveals about where you are seeking life apart from God.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I keep feeling discontent about... Underneath it I think I am looking for...

cards.title: What grief have you not spoken to God?
cards.body: Bring a sorrow you have kept silent into honest prayer. God can hold your questions and your tears.
cards.journalPlaceholder: A grief I have not spoken is... What I want to ask God is...

cards.title: What promise do you need to hold today?
cards.body: Find one promise of God that speaks to your current season, and write why your heart needs it now.
cards.journalPlaceholder: The promise I need to hold is... I need it because...

cards.title: Where is God asking for faithfulness, not results?
cards.body: Name a place you are tempted to give up because you cannot see the fruit, and consider what faithful obedience looks like there.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I am tempted to give up on... Faithfulness there would look like...

cards.title: Who might God be sending you toward?
cards.body: Consider the people God has placed in your ordinary paths, and who might be one He is drawing to Himself.
cards.journalPlaceholder: A person God has placed near me is... A next step of love toward them is...

cards.title: What would it take to truly rest?
cards.body: Consider what you are afraid will fall apart if you stop, and what it would mean to trust God with it enough to rest.
cards.journalPlaceholder: I am afraid that if I rest... What I want to entrust to God is...

cards.title: No condemnation
cards.body: Review this verse today. Say it aloud, type it from memory, then read it in context.

cards.title: Do not be anxious
cards.body: Review this verse today. Speak it slowly as a prayer, then read the surrounding passage.

cards.title: Trust in the Lord
cards.body: Review this verse today. Say it aloud, then write it from memory before checking the text.

cards.title: A way of escape
cards.body: Review this verse today. Let it become a promise you can recall the next time you are tempted.

cards.title: The Lord is my shepherd
cards.body: Review this verse today. Say it aloud as an anchor, then read the whole psalm slowly.

cards.title: Saved by grace for good works
cards.body: Review this verse today. Notice that you are saved by grace and created for the good works God prepared.

cards.title: Love one another
cards.body: Review this verse today. Ask God to help you love one specific person the way Jesus loves you.

cards.title: Seek first the kingdom
cards.body: Review this verse today. Let it reorder your worries by putting God's kingdom first.

cards.title: Study the word: abide
cards.body: In John 15, trace how Jesus connects remaining in Him with receiving His words, keeping His commands, and bearing fruit.

cards.title: Study the word: steadfast love
cards.body: Explore the Hebrew word hesed, God's covenant love. Notice how its repetition shapes the way these passages describe God.

cards.title: Study the word: shalom
cards.body: Trace the Hebrew word shalom, a peace that means wholeness and flourishing, and see how it points forward to the Prince of Peace.

cards.title: Study the word: repent
cards.body: Look at the Greek word metanoia, a change of mind that turns the whole life. See how Jesus and the apostles call people to it.

cards.title: Study the word: love
cards.body: Explore the Greek word agape, self-giving love. Notice how these passages define it by action rather than feeling.

cards.title: Study the word: justified
cards.body: Study the Greek word dikaioo, to be declared righteous. Trace how Paul roots this in faith and the finished work of Christ.

cards.title: Notice God's work
cards.body: Look back over the week before you rush into the next one.
questions: Where did you see God at work this week?
What truth from Scripture stayed with you?
What is one reason to give thanks?

cards.title: Examine and confess
cards.body: Invite God to search your week honestly, then receive His grace.
questions: Where did you fall short this week?
What does God's grace say over that failure?
What one change will you ask God to work in you?

cards.title: Renew your dependence
cards.body: Consider where you leaned on yourself this week, and turn again to God.
questions: Where did you try to manage life apart from God?
What are you carrying that you need to hand back to Him?
What is one way you will seek Him first this week?

cards.title: Check your loves
cards.body: Where your treasure is, your heart follows. Look at what captured your attention this week.
questions: What did most of your time and attention go to this week?
Where might a good thing be taking God's place?
What would it look like to reorder your loves around Him?

cards.title: Tend your relationships
cards.body: Look back at how you loved the people God placed around you this week.
questions: Is there a relationship where you need to pursue peace?
Whom do you need to forgive, or ask forgiveness from?
Who could you encourage in the week ahead?

cards.title: Look ahead in hope
cards.body: Set your eyes on Jesus before the new week begins.
questions: What weight do you want to lay aside going into this week?
Where do you need endurance right now?
How does looking to Jesus change the week ahead?
